neighbours.label: in a legal obligation clause (shall take, be reimbursed for, subject to), the word right before a 'reasonable/appropriate/any and all' qualifier
fire: Upon notice of a breach, the supplier shall take all reasonable measures to cure it.
The licensee shall use commercially reasonable efforts to market the product.
The employer shall be reimbursed by the contractor for any and all expenses incurred.
This right is subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.
The agency shall take appropriate action under its existing authority.
Each party shall make reasonable efforts to resolve any dispute informally.
The tenant shall indemnify the landlord against any and all claims arising from the use of the premises.
Members shall act in good faith and with reasonable care in all dealings.
quiet: After the breach was noticed, the supplier sent a technician the next morning.
The licensee printed new posters to market the product in the spring.
The contractor kept the receipts for the expenses in a blue folder.
This right was first written down in a charter from the twelfth century.
The agency moved its offices to a new building downtown last year.
Both parties met for lunch to talk about the dispute in person.
The tenant painted the kitchen and planted roses near the premises.
Members gathered in the hall and talked about their weekend plans.

notes: Top examples: 'shall take | all reasonable steps', 'reimbursed for | any and all', 'subject to | reasonable limitations'; output promotes ' reasonable', ' legitimate', ' valid'. Near misses are the same topics told as plain narrative without an obligation clause.
